title: Runtime kernel portfolio manager: online cost models for arch & seq-len aware selection
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Design and implement a lightweight runtime 'kernel portfolio manager' that maintains per-host and per-model cost models to pick the best kernel variant at prefill and decode time. The manager combines an offline candidate catalog with online micro-profiling and a fast decision layer to pick kernels that minimize latency P95 and token cost while respecting memory constraints.

Background & motivation: Current kernel selection is static or heuristic-driven and doesn't adapt to real traffic distributions (variable seq-len, batch shapes) or heterogeneous fleets (A100/RTX/TPU-like variants). This causes suboptimal tail latency and higher token cost for many workloads. We need an automated, low-overhead approach that continuously learns which kernel variant to use given (arch, seq_len, batch_size, dtype, quantization) and falls back gracefully.

Goals:
- Reduce P95 generation latency by 10-20% for tail-heavy workloads without increasing average token cost by >5%.
- Keep runtime decision overhead < 300us per request.
- Provide transparent metrics (per-model kernel choice frequency, decision confidence, microprofile samples).
- Safe rollout capability with canary/rollback and manual pinning.

Non-goals: Replace full offline autotuner; do not require long offline profiling runs. Not aiming to change kernel implementations themselves (separate work).

Approach: three-layer system: (1) Candidate Catalog - offline curated set of kernel variants with nominal hardware tags, memory footprints and expected strengths (prefill-optimized, decode-optimized, fused-attention). (2) Lightweight micro-profiling - when a model first sees a traffic pattern (seq_len bucket + batch shape + dtype), schedule short micro-benchmarks under production traffic shadowing (2-5 runs per candidate) to estimate mean latency and memory headroom. Profiling is budgeted and throttled by per-model rate limits. (3) Online cost model & chooser - a compact cost function combines latency estimate, memory safety margin, and token cost multiplier to compute an expected utility score per candidate. The highest-scoring candidate is selected, with exploration probability decaying over time.

Decision heuristics:
- Primary features: architecture family, GPU topology tag, seq_len bucket, batch_size, dtype, KV cache hit ratio.
- Use monotonic penalties for memory headroom < 10%.
- Penalize candidates with prior observed QoS violations.
- Exploration: epsilon-greedy tied to confidence interval of latency estimate; initial epsilon=0.15 for new seq_len buckets, decays to 0.02 over 24 hours.

Caching & TTLs: choice cached per (model, arch, seq_len_bucket, batch_bucket) with TTL=30m; explicit invalidation on rollout or kernel upgrade. Short TTLs for high-variance workloads.

Safety & fallback: if any sampled execution hits OOM/eviction/memory-pressure or latency SLO breach, mark candidate as unsafe for 15 minutes and fallback to conservative kernel (lowest memory footprint).

Instrumentation & metrics: emit per-decision event with features, chosen_candidate, score_breakdown, sample_latencies. Dashboards: kernel-choice heatmaps, P50/P95/P99 by kernel, microprofile success rates, exploration fraction. Alerting on increased fallback rate and customer-impacting regressions.

Rollout plan: implement feature-flagged canary on 10% of traffic for low-risk models for 2 weeks, run A/B with baseline static selection. Expand to 50% then 100% if no regression. Provide manual overrides in console.

Success criteria: meet latency goals on benchmark corpus (internal benchmarks + customer traces), no increase in SLO breaches during canary, clear cost benefit on token-level economics for selected workloads.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to only cover GPU-accelerated kernels and seq_len buckets [1, 32, 128, 512, 2048]. Prioritized prefill vs decode policies separately.

2026-02-18 - Design review (ENG + PM): agreed to keep micro-profiling budgeted (max 0.1% of requests) and to shadow profile on warm hosts to avoid cold-start artifacts. Action: add rate limiter to profiler.

2026-02-24 - Prototype: implemented candidate catalog loader and simple cost function. Measuring baseline samples on canary cluster; initial results show 12% P95 reduction on chat-heavy traces when choosing decode-optimized kernels for seq_len 128.

2026-02-28 - Feedback from Reliability: raised concern about profiling causing transient GC spikes on hosts. Mitigation: move micro-profiling to isolated execution lanes with throttled mem usage; added safety delay between profiling runs.
2026-03-02 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7654 (kernel-portfolio-manager MVP). Contains initial chooser, catalog schema, and logging hooks.

2026-03-04 - Performance team notes: need to add KW variance estimators and calibration for GPU-mode switch overheads (e.g., switching tensor cores/quantized kernels costs more on some GPUs). Planned change in next iteration.
2026-03-04 - PM approval: proceed to canary on dedicated dev environment (dev-cluster-2) with 5 labeled internal models. Linked canary checklist in attachments.
